newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish tobacco tax falls 2 bln SKR short-paper.
newsitem.headline: Swedish tobacco tax falls 2 bln SKR short-paper.

text.p: Swedish tax revenue from tobacco products will fall about two billion crowns short of government estimates in last autumn's budget, a Swedish newspaper said on Tuesday.

The government calculated it would raise 9.3 billion crowns from tobacco in 1997 by lifting taxes by 23 percent at the start of the year. It lowered this forecast to 8.5 billion crowns in its spring budget.

This income compares with usual annual revenue of 7.5 billion crowns. The additional money was to be spent on the battle to lower unemployment, currently running at 8.8 percent, and to finance tax reduction on beer.

But the daily Svenska Dagbladet said this income has already plunged by 10 percent and will fall further with another hike in taxes on tobacco due on August 1 which the government hoped would raise another 525 million crowns.
The newspaper said it calculated only 3.6 billion crowns were raised from tobacco tax in the first half of 1997 which would mean 7.2 billion crowns for the full year.
Svenska Dagbladet said it was unclear whether the fall in tax revenue was due to people giving up smoking or managing to acquire cigarettes which were not taxed, such as those smuggled into Sweden.
